headline: Fed 10-2 hold, 2y 4.67% overnight, NDX futures -1.2%, Alphabet -10% pre-market, Microsoft +3%
stance: Warsh's hold: 2y bought, long end sold, December back to the data. Hyperscalers now trade on free cash flow, not capex guides.

news.head: Alphabet -10% pre-market, free cash flow -$9.1bn
news.body: EPS $2.12 vs $3.02; revenue $127.6bn in line; cloud +103%. Capex $51.4bn, FY guide held, 2027 higher. Long-term debt $125bn vs $22bn y/y (~4:50am ET).

news.head: Microsoft +3% pre-market, Azure +48%, capex below
news.body: Revenue $92.3bn vs $90.7bn; EPS $4.89 vs $4.72. Capex $45.2bn vs $50.7bn expected on delayed third-party capacity. Azure guided 49-50% (~5:50am ET).

news.head: Samsung -4.1% Seoul on record profit, revenue miss
news.body: Operating profit 107tn won, 9x y/y, a 4th straight record; revenue 195tn won vs 207tn consensus. Shareholder-return plan disappointed (~4:30am ET).

news.head: Marvell -10% after hours on Lumentum talks; Shell +3%
news.body: Lumentum +10% after hours on the report. Shell: adjusted earnings $10.8bn, $5bn buyback, record refining margins. Lloyds -3.4%, low-quality beat (~5am ET).

implications: Memory bought on results, hyperscalers judged on cash. The AI capex bid now needs the spender to fund it from operations. Tonight's prints get the same test.
Two dissents and no guidance: Warsh handed December to the data. Core PCE and Q3 GDP at 8:30 are the first of it; a 0.4% core print undoes Wednesday's 2y rally.

watch.head: ECB 8:15, Lagarde 8:45; hold at 2.50% expected
watch.body: Two hikes since June, none priced today; France and Lagarde's term are the presser risk. Euro 1.1155, off a 1.1169 post-Fed high (~6am ET).

watch.head: GDP, PCE, claims 8:30
watch.body: Q3 GDP consensus 3.2%, core PCE 0.3% m/m. Claims 194K last week. A hot core reprices December faster than Warsh did.

watch.head: Amazon, Intel, SanDisk after today's close
watch.body: Same test as Wednesday: cloud growth and capex against free cash flow. Memory has carried the chip bid for 3 sessions; SanDisk is the read.

watch.head: BoJ overnight, ECI Fri 8:30; BoE Nov 5; midterms Nov 3
watch.body: BoJ hold at 1.25% expected after last month's hike; yen 157.86 (~6am ET). BoE priced to hike to 4%. US officials say Iran strikes may resume after Nov 3.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: Fed held 3.75-4.00%, 10-2; Cook and Hammack wanted 25bp. Warsh refused forward guidance; December hike odds 78% from 84% pre-meeting.
2y 4.67%, 10y 4.99% (~5:30am ET). 2y traded 4.79% on the statement and 4.69% after Warsh; 10y and 30y still closed higher Wednesday.
Brent $114.54, -0.7%; WTI $101.81, -0.9% (~6am ET) on Vance's outreach to Tehran. Gilts rallied on the budget: issuance GBP250.6bn, less long-dated; 2027 inflation seen 3.4%.
sections.positioning: COT Oct 20: WTI specs 14th percentile, new this week, -4 points w/w; spot at the 98th. Extended short into $100 crude. 2y specs 99th a 13th week, background to Wednesday's rally.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: Nasdaq 100 futures -1.2%, S&P -0.4%, Dow +0.4% (~4:40am ET). Wednesday: S&P +0.3%, a 3rd straight gain; semis +1.75%, real estate -0.7%.
Asia split on the same chip news. Nikkei +1.1%, Kospi -1.2% after Wednesday's +6.6%, Taiex -1.4%, Hang Seng -0.6% at the close.
Hyperscaler prints split on free cash flow, not capex: -10% and +3% after hours. Semis and neoclouds fell with both.
sections.positioning: COT Oct 20: nothing new in equities. Russell 2000 specs 100th percentile a 4th week, Nasdaq 100 97th a 5th. The extended long meets a -1.2% futures open.

single_name.note: New to the screen today: 2 insider rules fired, trade above its 200-day line, 7.4 days to cover. Insider buy filed Oct 9; signal aging, 75% weight left.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: IG at these spreads has been tighter only 4% of the time in 25 years. No cushion if December reprices.
Supply is the AI credit risk. Hyperscaler and data-center bonds $368bn year to date, 6x last year. All issuers $6.61tn, +15%, a record with 2 months left.
sections.positioning: COT Oct 20: HY specs 13th percentile, new this week, -15 points w/w; dealer IG inventory 19th. Shorts built into September's record $54bn HY month and the widening after it.

single_name.note: Muni credit closed-end fund, new to the screen Tuesday. 2 insider rules fired, trade above its 200-day line, insider buy filed Oct 27. Munis cheapened on issuance, retail outflows.
